```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Kaikousidis_2023_donepezil_combined_mouse"))$reference`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics15051409>

Kaikousidis et al. (2023) modelled serum and brain donepezil concentrations in
mice after an oral solution and after a nasal film, in four stages. Each stage
was fitted twice, once to the per-time-point mean concentrations and once to
the raw concentrations of every animal pooled as one typical subject. The
library carries the five models the paper reports with full parameter tables:

```{r models}
stems <- c(
  oral_mean = "Kaikousidis_2023_donepezil_oral_meandata_mouse",
  oral_raw = "Kaikousidis_2023_donepezil_oral_rawdata_mouse",
  in_mean = "Kaikousidis_2023_donepezil_intranasal_meandata_mouse",
  in_raw = "Kaikousidis_2023_donepezil_intranasal_rawdata_mouse",
  combined = "Kaikousidis_2023_donepezil_combined_mouse"
)
mods <- lapply(stems, function(s) rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb(s)))
tibble::tibble(
  Model = unname(stems),
  Source = c(
    "Table 2, Per Os - Mean Data", "Table 2, Per Os - Raw Data",
    "Table 3, IN - Mean Data", "Table 3, IN - Raw Data",
    "Table 4, Total Fit (Per Os + IN raw data)"
  )
) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

* **Oral models** (Figure 2): first-order absorption from a gut `depot` into
  blood (`central`), a blood-peripheral exchange, a one-way blood-to-brain
  transfer `k_central_brain` (paper `k23`) that depletes blood, and a lumped
  brain elimination `keff_brain` (paper `k30`). The blood volume is fixed to
  0.279 L from the paper's preliminary blood-only fit (Table 1), which makes
  the brain volume identifiable.
* **Intranasal models** (Figure 4): the nasal-film dose in `depot_nasal` is
  split into a fraction `P1` absorbed into blood, a fraction `(1 - P1) * P2`
  absorbed directly into brain (both zero-order over `Tk0` after a lag
  `Tlag`), and the remainder `(1 - P1) * (1 - P2)`, which reaches brain after a
  Savic transit chain (mean transit time `Mtt`, rate `ktr`) and a first-order
  absorption step out of `depot_brain` (`ka`). There is no peripheral
  compartment. `k23` and `k30` are fixed to the oral values of the matching
  data representation.
* **Combined model** (Section 3.3): both sub-models fitted jointly to the raw
  data, sharing the blood elimination, blood-to-brain and brain elimination
  rate constants, with route-specific apparent volumes and residual errors
  selected by `ROUTE_ORAL` (1 = oral, 0 = nasal film). The authors present it
  as a check on the robustness of the staged fits and did not refine it
  further.

None of the models estimates between-animal variability: each is a
typical-value model with residual error only.

# Population

Eight-week-old C57BL/6J mice (Section 2.1) received either 0.2 mL of a
1.25 mg/mL donepezil solution by gastric gavage (0.25 mg, 10 mg/kg) or one
nasal film containing 0.1 mg donepezil (4 mg/kg), which implies a body weight
of about 25 g. Serum and perfused brain were sampled destructively at 5-360 min
after the oral dose (n >= 5 per time point) and at 5-120 min after the nasal
film (n = 3-5 per time point). Sex and the total number of animals are not
reported. Concentrations below the LOQ (serum 0.043 ug/mL, brain 0.038 ug/mL)
were set to LOQ/2 for fitting.

The same information is available programmatically, e.g.
`readModelDb("Kaikousidis_2023_donepezil_combined_mouse")()$population`.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its table row. The table
below collects the typical values of all five models, back-transformed from the
packaged files, next to the paper symbol and source table.

```{r source-trace}
back_transform <- function(name, est) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    grepl("^logit", name) ~ 1 / (1 + exp(-est)),
    grepl("Sd", name) ~ est^2,
    grepl("^l", name) ~ exp(est),
    TRUE ~ est
  )
}
symbols <- tibble::tribble(
  ~name, ~symbol,
  "lka", "k12 (1/min)",
  "lkel", "k20 (1/min)",
  "lk_central_brain", "k23 (1/min)",
  "lk12", "k24 (1/min)",
  "lk21", "k42 (1/min)",
  "lkeff_brain", "k30 (1/min)",
  "lvc", "Vblood / V1 (L)",
  "lvc_oral", "Vblood, oral (L)",
  "lvc_intranasal", "Vblood_IN (L)",
  "lv_brain", "Vbrain / V2 (L)",
  "lv_brain_oral", "Vbrain_PO (L)",
  "lv_brain_intranasal", "Vbrain_IN (L)",
  "ltlag", "Tlag (min)",
  "ld1", "Tk0 (min)",
  "lmtt", "Mtt (min)",
  "lktr", "ktr (1/min)",
  "logitfrel", "P1",
  "logitfrel2", "P2",
  "lka_brain", "ka (1/min)",
  "propSd", "b1 (variance)",
  "propSd_Cbrain", "b2 (variance)",
  "addSd", "a1 (variance)",
  "addSd_Cbrain", "a2 (variance)",
  "addSd_oral", "a1 (variance)",
  "addSd_Cbrain_oral", "a2 (variance)",
  "addSd_intranasal", "a3 (variance)",
  "propSd_Cbrain_intranasal", "b1 (variance)"
)
trace <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(names(mods), function(m) {
  mods[[m]]$iniDf |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(ntheta)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(model = m, name, value = signif(back_transform(name, est), 3),
                     fixed = fix)
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(value = ifelse(fixed, paste0(value, " (fixed)"), as.character(value))) |>
  dplyr::select(-fixed) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = model, values_from = value, values_fill = "") |>
  dplyr::left_join(symbols, by = "name") |>
  dplyr::relocate(symbol, .after = name)
stopifnot(!anyNA(trace$symbol))
trace |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Parameter" = name, "Paper symbol" = symbol,
    "Oral, mean (Table 2)" = oral_mean, "Oral, raw (Table 2)" = oral_raw,
    "IN, mean (Table 3)" = in_mean, "IN, raw (Table 3)" = in_raw,
    "Combined (Table 4)" = combined
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Typical values on the paper's scale. Residual-error rows show the tabulated variance (the model stores its square root).")
```

| Equation | Source location |
|----------|-----------------|
| Oral structure: depot -> blood (k12), blood <-> peripheral (k24, k42), blood -> brain (k23), elimination from blood (k20) and brain (k30) | Figure 2; Section 3.1 |
| Intranasal structure: depot -> blood and depot -> brain with `Tk0` and `Tlag`; depot -> transit chain -> Abs -> brain (`ktr`, `ka`); blood -> brain (k23); elimination k20, k30 | Figure 4; Section 3.2 |
| Dose split `F2 = P2`, `F3 = (1 - P2) * P3`, `F4 = (1 - P2) * (1 - P3)` | Section 3.2 (printed as `P1`, `P2` in Tables 3-4) |
| Transit count `N` from `ktr = (N + 1) / Mtt` (8.58 and 10.14 transit compartments) | Section 3.2 |
| Residual error: proportional / additive per matrix and fit | Sections 3.1-3.3; Tables 2-4 |

The transit count is not a parameter of the files: it follows from `Mtt` and
`ktr`. The paper reports N = 8.58 (mean data) and 10.14 (raw data). These equal
`ktr * Mtt - 1` for both fits, i.e. the Savic relation `ktr = (N + 1) / Mtt`;
the formula as printed, `(N - 1) / Mtt`, would give 10.58 and 12.14.

```{r transit-count}
ntr <- function(m) {
  th <- mods[[m]]$theta
  exp(th[["lmtt"]]) * exp(th[["lktr"]]) - 1
}
n_check <- c(in_mean = ntr("in_mean"), in_raw = ntr("in_raw"), combined = ntr("combined"))
round(n_check, 2)
stopifnot(abs(n_check[["in_mean"]] - 8.58) < 0.01, abs(n_check[["in_raw"]] - 10.14) < 0.01)
```

# Simulation

All five models are deterministic at the typical value, so one simulated
mouse per route reproduces the paper's fitted curves. Doses are 0.25 mg into
`depot` (oral) and 0.1 mg into `depot_nasal` (nasal film). Each model has two
observation endpoints (`Cc` for serum, `Cbrain` for brain), so the
observation rows carry `dvid = 1`; rxode2 returns both concentrations on every
row.

```{r simulate}
make_events <- function(route, tend, by = 0.5) {
  dose <- if (route == "oral") {
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 0.25, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  } else {
    data.frame(id = 1L, time = 0, amt = 0.1, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot_nasal", dvid = NA_integer_)
  }
  obs <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq(0, tend, by = by), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
                    cmt = NA_character_, dvid = 1L)
  ev <- rbind(dose, obs)
  ev$ROUTE_ORAL <- as.integer(route == "oral")
  ev
}
runs <- tibble::tribble(
  ~fit, ~model, ~route, ~tend, ~figure,
  "Oral, mean data", "oral_mean", "oral", 360, "Figure 3A (upper)",
  "Oral, raw data", "oral_raw", "oral", 360, "Figure 3A (lower)",
  "IN, mean data", "in_mean", "intranasal", 120, "Figure 5A (upper)",
  "IN, raw data", "in_raw", "intranasal", 120, "Figure 5A (lower)",
  "Combined, oral", "combined", "oral", 360, "Figure 6 (upper)",
  "Combined, IN", "combined", "intranasal", 120, "Figure 6 (lower)"
)
sim <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(runs)), function(i) {
  ev <- make_events(runs$route[i], runs$tend[i])
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mods[[runs$model[i]]], events = ev))
  s$fit <- runs$fit[i]
  s$route <- runs$route[i]
  s
})) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = runs$fit))
# Integration noise only: states never go meaningfully negative.
stopifnot(all(sim$Cc >= -1e-6), all(sim$Cbrain >= -1e-6))
```

## Checks of the intranasal input

The intranasal files write the lagged zero-order release and the transit
input as explicit functions of the nasal-film dose (`podo()` / `tad()` of
`depot_nasal`) rather than with `f()`, `alag()` and `dur()` on three dose
records. A two-endpoint model with a modelled `dur()` does not solve in
rxode2 5.1.8 ("Duration is zero/negative"). The check below solves the
intranasal mean-data model against an independent single-endpoint
formulation that uses rxode2's own lag, duration and bioavailability on three
dose records, and confirms mass balance with elimination switched off.

```{r input-check}
th <- mods$in_mean$theta
ref_mod <- rxode2::rxode2({
  ntr <- mtt * ktr - 1
  t_tr <- tad(depot_brain)
  transit_in <- 0
  if (t_tr > 0) transit_in <- (1 - p1) * (1 - p2) * exp(log(podo(depot_brain)) + log(ktr) + ntr * log(ktr * t_tr) - ktr * t_tr - lgamma(ntr + 1))
  d/dt(depot_brain) <- transit_in - ka_brain * depot_brain
  d/dt(central) <- -(kel + k_central_brain) * central
  d/dt(brain) <- ka_brain * depot_brain + k_central_brain * central - keff_brain * brain
  f(depot_brain) <- 0
  f(central) <- p1
  alag(central) <- tlag
  dur(central) <- d1
  f(brain) <- (1 - p1) * p2
  alag(brain) <- tlag
  dur(brain) <- d1
  Cc <- central / vc
  Cbrain <- brain / v_brain
})
ref_par <- c(
  mtt = exp(th[["lmtt"]]), ktr = exp(th[["lktr"]]), tlag = exp(th[["ltlag"]]),
  d1 = exp(th[["ld1"]]), p1 = plogis(th[["logitfrel"]]), p2 = plogis(th[["logitfrel2"]]),
  ka_brain = exp(th[["lka_brain"]]), kel = exp(th[["lkel"]]),
  k_central_brain = exp(th[["lk_central_brain"]]), keff_brain = exp(th[["lkeff_brain"]]),
  vc = exp(th[["lvc"]]), v_brain = exp(th[["lv_brain"]])
)
ref_ev <- rxode2::et(amt = 0.1, cmt = "central", rate = -2) |>
  rxode2::et(amt = 0.1, cmt = "brain", rate = -2) |>
  rxode2::et(amt = 0.1, cmt = "depot_brain") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 120, by = 0.5))
ref <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(ref_mod, params = ref_par, events = ref_ev))
pkg <- sim |> dplyr::filter(fit == "IN, mean data")
stopifnot(identical(ref$time, pkg$time))
rel_dev <- c(
  Cc = max(abs(pkg$Cc - ref$Cc)) / max(ref$Cc),
  Cbrain = max(abs(pkg$Cbrain - ref$Cbrain)) / max(ref$Cbrain)
)
signif(rel_dev, 2)
# Two independent ODE solutions at the default tolerances (rtol 1e-6);
# the observed agreement is about 1e-6.
stopifnot(all(rel_dev < 1e-3))

# Mass balance: with blood and brain elimination switched off the whole
# 0.1 mg dose ends up in the model states.
mb <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(
  mods$in_mean, events = make_events("intranasal", 600),
  params = c(lkel = -40, lkeff_brain = -40)
))
mass_end <- with(mb[nrow(mb), ], depot_nasal + depot_brain + central + brain)
mass_end
stopifnot(abs(mass_end / 0.1 - 1) < 1e-4)
```

The dose split implied by the fractions, compared with the Discussion's
summary (direct-to-blood about half the dose, delayed transit fraction
25-30%):

```{r dose-split}
split <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(c("in_mean", "in_raw", "combined"), function(m) {
  th <- mods[[m]]$theta
  p1 <- plogis(th[["logitfrel"]])
  p2 <- plogis(th[["logitfrel2"]])
  tibble::tibble(model = m, blood = p1, direct_brain = (1 - p1) * p2,
                 transit_brain = (1 - p1) * (1 - p2))
}))
split |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(-model, \(x) round(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Model" = model, "Direct to blood" = blood,
                "Direct to brain" = direct_brain, "Transit to brain" = transit_brain) |>
  knitr::kable()
stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(split[, -1]) - 1) < 1e-12))
```

# Replicate published figures

The points are values the maintainers read off the fitted curves in the
paper's figures (peaks, the intranasal brain trough between the two peaks,
and selected late times); the lines are the packaged models.

```{r figure-reads}
fig_reads <- tibble::tribble(
  ~fit, ~matrix, ~time, ~value,
  "Oral, mean data", "Blood", 17, 0.355,
  "Oral, mean data", "Brain", 20, 0.215,
  "Oral, mean data", "Blood", 120, 0.065,
  "Oral, mean data", "Brain", 120, 0.045,
  "Oral, mean data", "Blood", 360, 0.022,
  "Oral, raw data", "Blood", 17, 0.355,
  "Oral, raw data", "Brain", 20, 0.215,
  "IN, mean data", "Blood", 15, 1.85,
  "IN, mean data", "Brain", 15, 1.03,
  "IN, mean data", "Brain", 30, 0.27,
  "IN, mean data", "Brain", 60, 0.49,
  "IN, raw data", "Blood", 15, 1.80,
  "IN, raw data", "Brain", 15, 0.97,
  "IN, raw data", "Brain", 30, 0.25,
  "IN, raw data", "Brain", 60, 0.50,
  "Combined, oral", "Blood", 17, 0.355,
  "Combined, oral", "Brain", 20, 0.23,
  "Combined, IN", "Blood", 15, 1.75,
  "Combined, IN", "Brain", 15, 1.00,
  "Combined, IN", "Brain", 60, 0.50
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = runs$fit))

sim_long <- sim |>
  dplyr::select(fit, time, Blood = Cc, Brain = Cbrain) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(Blood, Brain), names_to = "matrix", values_to = "conc")
```

```{r figure-3-5-6, fig.width = 7.5, fig.height = 9}
ggplot(sim_long, aes(time, conc, colour = matrix)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_point(data = fig_reads, aes(time, value), shape = 21, fill = "white", size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~fit, ncol = 2, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(Blood = "#1f77b4", Brain = "#2ca02c")) +
  labs(x = "Time (min)", y = "Donepezil (ug/mL)", colour = NULL,
       caption = "Replicates Figures 3A, 5A and 6 of Kaikousidis 2023 (fitted curves).") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r figure-check}
fig_check <- fig_reads |>
  dplyr::left_join(sim_long, by = c("fit", "matrix", "time")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (conc / value - 1))
fig_check |>
  dplyr::mutate(conc = signif(conc, 3), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Fit" = fit, "Matrix" = matrix, "Time (min)" = time,
                "Read from figure (ug/mL)" = value, "Model (ug/mL)" = conc,
                "% diff" = pct_diff) |>
  knitr::kable()
# Typical-value solves, no random draws: every model point sits within 12%
# of the curve read off the paper's figure (largest 11%, the shallow brain
# trough at 30 min). Fixing the raw-data intranasal fit's k23/k30 to the
# mean-data oral values instead moves its first brain peak by +34%.
stopifnot(!anyNA(fig_check$conc), all(abs(fig_check$pct_diff) < 15))
```

The intranasal brain curve shows the paper's double peak: the direct
nose-to-brain input peaks at the end of the zero-order window
(`Tlag + Tk0`, about 15 min) and the transit-delayed input produces the second
peak near 60 min.

```{r double-peak}
second_peak <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(route == "intranasal", time > 30) |>
  dplyr::group_by(fit) |>
  dplyr::summarise(t_second_peak = time[which.max(Cbrain)], .groups = "drop")
second_peak
stopifnot(all(second_peak$t_second_peak > 45 & second_peak$t_second_peak < 75))
```

# PKNCA validation

Non-compartmental analysis of the typical curves, one PKNCA block per matrix,
grouped by fit. The oral curves end at the last oral sample (360 min) and the
intranasal curves at the last intranasal sample (120 min).

```{r pknca}
run_nca <- function(conc_col) {
  conc <- sim |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    dplyr::transmute(id = 1L, fit = as.character(fit), time, conc = pmax(.data[[conc_col]], 0))
  stopifnot(all(conc |> dplyr::group_by(fit) |> dplyr::summarise(t0 = min(time)) |> dplyr::pull(t0) == 0))
  dose <- runs |>
    dplyr::transmute(id = 1L, fit, time = 0, amt = ifelse(route == "oral", 0.25, 0.1))
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | fit + id)
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose, amt ~ time | fit + id)
  intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = Inf, cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
  PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
}
nca_blood <- run_nca("Cc")
nca_brain <- run_nca("Cbrain")
nca_tab <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(nca_blood) |> dplyr::mutate(matrix = "Blood"),
  as.data.frame(nca_brain) |> dplyr::mutate(matrix = "Brain")
) |>
  dplyr::select(fit, matrix, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES) |>
  dplyr::mutate(fit = factor(fit, levels = runs$fit)) |>
  dplyr::arrange(matrix, fit)
nca_tab |>
  dplyr::mutate(cmax = signif(cmax, 3), auclast = signif(auclast, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Fit" = fit, "Matrix" = matrix, "Cmax (ug/mL)" = cmax,
                "Tmax (min)" = tmax, "AUClast (ug*min/mL)" = auclast) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

## Comparison against published values

The Discussion reports that after the nasal film both serum and brain reach
their maximum at the 15-min sampling time:

```{r nca-compare}
in_fits <- c("IN, mean data", "IN, raw data", "Combined, IN")
reference <- data.frame(fit = in_fits, tmax = 15)
cmp <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = as.data.frame(nca_blood) |> dplyr::filter(fit %in% in_fits),
    reference = reference, by = "fit", params = "tmax", units = c(tmax = "min")
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(Matrix = "Blood", .before = 2),
  nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
    simulated = as.data.frame(nca_brain) |> dplyr::filter(fit %in% in_fits),
    reference = reference, by = "fit", params = "tmax", units = c(tmax = "min")
  ) |> dplyr::mutate(Matrix = "Brain", .before = 2)
)
knitr::kable(cmp, caption = "Simulated vs. published Tmax after the nasal film. * differs from reference by >20%.")
tmax_in <- nca_tab |> dplyr::filter(fit %in% in_fits) |> dplyr::pull(tmax)
stopifnot(all(abs(tmax_in - 15) <= 1.5))
```

The Discussion also quotes intranasal-to-oral ratios of Cmax and AUC from the
non-compartmental analysis of the observed data in the authors' earlier study
(Papakyriakopoulou et al. 2023): Cmax 3.9-fold (blood) and 5.7-fold (brain)
higher, and AUC 1.4-fold (blood) and 3.1-fold (brain) higher after the nasal
film, at a 2.5-fold lower dose. The model-based ratios are shown for
comparison; they are not a gate, because that analysis is of the observed
mean data rather than of these fitted curves, and the AUC interval of that
analysis is not stated.

```{r ratio-compare}
ratio <- function(oral_fit, in_fit) {
  nca_tab |>
    dplyr::filter(fit %in% c(oral_fit, in_fit)) |>
    dplyr::mutate(route = ifelse(fit == in_fit, "in", "oral")) |>
    dplyr::select(matrix, route, cmax, auclast) |>
    tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = route, values_from = c(cmax, auclast)) |>
    dplyr::transmute(matrix, cmax_ratio = cmax_in / cmax_oral,
                     auclast_ratio = auclast_in / auclast_oral)
}
ratios <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  ratio("Oral, mean data", "IN, mean data") |> dplyr::mutate(source = "Mean-data models"),
  ratio("Oral, raw data", "IN, raw data") |> dplyr::mutate(source = "Raw-data models"),
  ratio("Combined, oral", "Combined, IN") |> dplyr::mutate(source = "Combined model"),
  tibble::tibble(matrix = c("Blood", "Brain"), cmax_ratio = c(3.9, 5.7),
                 auclast_ratio = c(1.4, 3.1), source = "Reported (observed NCA)")
)
ratios |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(cmax_ratio, auclast_ratio), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::arrange(matrix) |>
  dplyr::rename("Matrix" = matrix, "Cmax IN / oral" = cmax_ratio,
                "AUC IN / oral" = auclast_ratio, "Source" = source) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

The model-based brain Cmax ratio (4.2-4.5) is lower than the reported
5.7-fold, and the blood Cmax ratio (5.3-5.6) is higher than the reported
3.9-fold. The model-based AUC ratios over each route's own sampling window
match the reported blood ratio for the separate fits (1.5 vs 1.4) and the
reported brain ratio for the combined fit (3.1 vs 3.1). The separate fits give
1.8-1.9 for brain, and the combined fit gives 2.6 for blood, because its
faster blood elimination shortens the oral serum curve. The paper does not
give the AUC interval or say whether the ratios are dose-normalised, so these
differences cannot be attributed to the model.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **Residual-error scale.** Tables 2-4 print the residual-error parameters
  (`a1`, `a2`, `a3`, `b1`, `b2`) without saying whether they are variances or
  standard deviations. The maintainers read them as NONMEM variances and store
  their square roots. Read as standard deviations, the oral raw-data additive
  error on serum (0.016 ug/mL) would put 90% of observations within
  +/-0.026 ug/mL of a 0.33 ug/mL peak. The raw serum data in Figure 3A
  (lower) span about 0.13-0.72 ug/mL around that peak, which matches the
  variance reading (SD 0.126 ug/mL, 90% interval about 0.12-0.54 ug/mL).
  The intranasal raw serum data (Figure 5A, lower: about 0.2-1.3 ug/mL at
  30 min) likewise fit an SD of sqrt(0.082) = 0.29 ug/mL better than
  0.082 ug/mL. The proportional rows are read on the same scale.
- **Mislabelled table blocks.** Table 3 prints its residual-error block under
  "Per Os" headings, although the block sits in the intranasal table and has
  the intranasal structure the text describes (additive serum, proportional
  brain). Table 4's footnote labels `b1` / `b2` as intranasal blood / brain,
  but the table rows are `a1`, `a2`, `a3`, `b1`, and the text says the
  intranasal blood error is additive. The rows are assigned by the text: `a3`
  is the intranasal serum additive error and `b1` the intranasal brain
  proportional error, matching the separate intranasal raw-data fit
  (0.084 vs 0.082 and 0.236 vs 0.238).
- **Fraction notation.** Section 3.2 writes the dose split with `P2` (blood)
  and `P3` (direct brain), while Tables 3-4 print them as `P1` and `P2`, and
  the Table 4 footnote calls `P2` the "fraction of dose absorbed in brain".
  The packaged models follow the printed equation (`P2` is the share of the
  non-blood dose, not of the whole dose); where the paper's equation and its
  labels disagree, the maintainers follow the equation. The Discussion's
  figures of "25-30%" for the transit fraction and "20-25%" for the olfactory
  fraction match neither reading exactly.
- **Rate-constant labels in Section 3.2.** The text says that "the blood-to-brain
  transfer (k23) and the brain elimination (k20) were fixed ... while the blood
  elimination (k30) was taken as a prior". Figure 4 and the Table 3 footnote
  name k20 as blood elimination (estimated, 0.046 / 0.05 1/min) and k30 as
  brain elimination, so `k23` and `k30` are the fixed pair. The text does not
  say which oral fit supplied them. Fixing them to the matching data
  representation (mean to mean, raw to raw) reproduces Figure 5. The other
  pairing moves the raw-data intranasal brain peak from 0.95 to 1.28 ug/mL
  (Figure 5 about 0.97).
- **Oral blood volume in the combined fit.** Table 4 does not list the oral
  blood volume. It is taken as the fixed 0.279 L of the oral sub-model
  (Section 3.1), which reproduces the oral panels of Figure 6.
- **No peripheral compartment after intranasal dosing in the combined fit.**
  Section 3.3 joins "the two previous individual models", and the intranasal
  model (Figure 4) has no peripheral compartment. With the oral peripheral
  exchange also applied to intranasal dosing, the combined model's intranasal
  serum peak would drop from 1.77 to 1.63 ug/mL and the curve would keep a
  slow tail (0.05 ug/mL at 120 min) that Figure 6 does not show.
- **Transit relation.** The printed `ktr = (N - 1) / Mtt` is read as
  `ktr = (N + 1) / Mtt`, the only form that reproduces the reported
  N = 8.58 and 10.14 (checked above).
- **Lag time and duration in the combined fit.** Table 4 reports `Tlag` and
  `Tk0` with relative standard errors of 0.11% and 0.06%. They are estimates,
  not fixed values, and are packaged as estimated.
- **Single nasal-film dose.** The explicit intranasal input is keyed on the
  most recent `depot_nasal` dose (`podo()` / `tad()`). The models are valid
  for the single doses the paper studied, or for doses spaced beyond the
  transit chain (about 3 x `Mtt`).
- **Preliminary blood-only fit not packaged.** The two-compartment fit to
  the oral serum data (Table 1) is the first stage of the oral model and only
  serves to fix the blood volume. It is not packaged as a separate model.
- **No correction notice** for the article was found (search on 2026-10-26).
